data: Parent of the 160-m moonlet Dimorphos struck by NASA's DART on 2022-09-26 — the first demonstration of kinetic-impactor planetary defense. Didymos itself remained intact as a 780-m S-type observing the binary period change.

S-type binary asteroid system — Didymos is the 780-m parent with the 160-m moonlet Dimorphos in 11.9-hour orbit at 1.2 km separation. NASA's DART hit Dimorphos in September 2022; Didymos remained intact while observing the kinetic-impact demonstration. ESA's Hera mission (launch 2024) will survey the post-impact system.
DART — NASA, 26 September 2022 (kinetic-impactor test on companion Dimorphos)
LICIACube — ASI, 2022 (CubeSat observation of impact ejecta)
Hera — ESA, en route 2026, arrival 2026 (impact aftermath survey)
Didymos is a binary near-Earth asteroid (semi-major axis 1.64 AU). DART (NASA, 2022) struck its small companion Dimorphos to test asteroid-deflection physics.
Half the longest diameter of the orbit ellipse — and the single number that sets the orbital period.
